name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQI_Q05 - Net force on an electric dipole in non-uniform field

questiontext.text:
Figure 1.5 shows electric field lines in which an electric dipole \(\mathbf{p}\) is placed as shown. Which of the following statements is correct?

चित्र 1.5 में वैद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएँ दर्शाई गई हैं जिनमें एक वैद्युत द्विध्रुव \(\mathbf{p}\) चित्रानुसार रखा गया है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
An electric dipole \(\mathbf{p}\) consisting of \(-q\) (on the left) and \(+q\) (on the right) is placed in an electric field whose field lines point towards the right and diverge as we move from left to right.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Closer spacing of electric field lines indicates a stronger electric field magnitude, while wider spacing indicates a weaker electric field magnitude.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electrostatic force on a charge \(q\) in an electric field \(\mathbf{E}\) is \(\mathbf{F} = q\mathbf{E}\). For a positive charge, the force is in the direction of \(\mathbf{E}\); for a negative charge, it is opposite to \(\mathbf{E}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Since the field lines are closer on the left and farther apart on the right, the electric field strength \(E_{-q}\) at the location of \(-q\) is greater than the electric field strength \(E_{+q}\) at the location of \(+q\):
\[E_{-q} > E_{+q}\]
The force on \(+q\) is \(F_{+q} = qE_{+q}\) directed towards the right.
The force on \(-q\) is \(F_{-q} = qE_{-q}\) directed towards the left.
Since \(qE_{-q} > qE_{+q}\), the leftward force dominates over the rightward force.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Therefore, the net force on the dipole is directed towards the left.

चरण 1: दिए गए आँकड़े और शर्तें
एक वैद्युत द्विध्रुव \(\mathbf{p}\), जिसमें \(-q\) (बाएँ) तथा \(+q\) (दाएँ) हैं, एक ऐसे वैद्युत क्षेत्र में रखा गया है जिसकी क्षेत्र रेखाएँ दाईं ओर इंगित हैं तथा बाएँ से दाएँ जाने पर अपसारित (फैलती) हो रही हैं।

चरण 2: मान्यताएँ और चिह्न परिपाटी
वैद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाओं का सघन होना अधिक प्रबल वैद्युत क्षेत्र तथा विरल होना अपेक्षाकृत दुर्बल वैद्युत क्षेत्र को दर्शाता है।

चरण 3: संबंधित सूत्र और सिद्धांत
वैद्युत क्षेत्र \(\mathbf{E}\) में स्थित आवेश \(q\) पर लगने वाला वैद्युत बल \(\mathbf{F} = q\mathbf{E}\) होता है। धनात्मक आवेश पर बल \(\mathbf{E}\) की दिशा में तथा ऋणात्मक आवेश पर \(\mathbf{E}\) के विपरीत दिशा में होता है।

चरण 4: चरणबद्ध हल
चूँकि बाईं ओर क्षेत्र रेखाएँ अधिक सघन और दाईं ओर अधिक विरल हैं, इसलिए \(-q\) के स्थान पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र की प्रबलता \(E_{-q}\), \(+q\) के स्थान पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र की प्रबलता \(E_{+q}\) से अधिक है:
\[E_{-q} > E_{+q}\]
\(+q\) पर लगने वाला बल \(F_{+q} = qE_{+q}\) दाईं ओर दिष्ट है।
\(-q\) पर लगने वाला बल \(F_{-q} = qE_{-q}\) बाईं ओर दिष्ट है।
चूँकि \(qE_{-q} > qE_{+q}\), इसलिए बाईं ओर लगने वाला बल दाईं ओर लगने वाले बल से अधिक है।

चरण 5: जाँच और अंतिम उत्तर
अतः द्विध्रुव पर नेट बल बाईं ओर लगेगा।

answer.text: The dipole will not experience any force.
The dipole will experience a force towards right.
The dipole will experience a force towards left.
The dipole will experience a force upwards.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQI_Q06 - Electric field on the other side of an isolated conducting plane

questiontext.text:
A point charge \(+q\), is placed at a distance \(d\) from an isolated conducting plane. The field at a point P on the other side of the plane is

एक बिंदु आवेश \(+q\), किसी विलगित चालक समतल से \(d\) दूरी पर रखा गया है। समतल के दूसरी ओर स्थित एक बिंदु P पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र की दिशा क्या होगी?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When a point charge \(+q\) is placed near an isolated neutral conducting plane, electrostatic induction occurs on the surfaces of the conductor. Negative charge is induced on the face of the plane facing \(+q\), and an equal amount of positive charge is induced on the opposite (far) face.

Step 2: Evaluation
The surface of a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is an equipotential surface, and the electric field lines must always be perpendicular to the surface of the conductor. Furthermore, electric field lines originate from positive charges.

Step 3: Application
Because positive charge is induced on the far side of the isolated conducting plane, the electric field lines at point P on the other side of the plane emerge normally from the conducting surface and point away from it.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the electric field at point P on the other side of the plane is directed perpendicular to the plane and away from the plane.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
जब किसी बिंदु आवेश \(+q\) को एक विलगित उदासीन चालक समतल के निकट रखा जाता है, तो चालक के पृष्ठों पर स्थिरवैद्युत प्रेरण होता है। \(+q\) के सामने वाले पृष्ठ पर ऋणात्मक आवेश प्रेरित हो जाता है तथा विपरीत (दूसरी) ओर के पृष्ठ पर समान मात्रा में धनात्मक आवेश प्रेरित हो जाता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
स्थिरवैद्युत संतुलन में किसी चालक का पृष्ठ एक समविभव पृष्ठ होता है और वैद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएँ सदैव चालक पृष्ठ के लंबवत होती हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त, वैद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएँ धनात्मक आवेशों से बाहर की ओर निकलती हैं।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
चूँकि विलगित चालक समतल की दूसरी ओर धनात्मक आवेश प्रेरित होता है, इसलिए समतल के दूसरी ओर स्थित बिंदु P पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएँ चालक पृष्ठ से अभिलंबवत बाहर की ओर निकलती हैं।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः समतल के दूसरी ओर बिंदु P पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र समतल के लंबवत तथा समतल से दूर की ओर दिष्ट होता है।

answer.text: directed perpendicular to the plane and away from the plane.
directed perpendicular to the plane but towards the plane.
directed radially away from the point charge.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQI_Q07 - Electric field on a diameter of a uniformly charged hemisphere

questiontext.text:
A hemisphere is uniformly charged positively. The electric field at a point on a diameter away from the centre is directed

एक अर्धगोला एकसमान रूप से धनावेशित है। इसके केंद्र से दूर किसी व्यास पर स्थित एक बिंदु पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र की दिशा होगी

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Consider a uniformly positively charged hemispherical shell lying above the equatorial plane (\(z \ge 0\)) with its circular base in the \(xy\)-plane. Inside a complete uniformly charged spherical shell, the net electric field at every point is zero.

Step 2: Evaluation
Let a complete uniformly charged spherical shell be composed of the upper hemisphere (\(z \ge 0\)) and the lower hemisphere (\(z \le 0\)). Consider any point \(P\) on a diameter in the \(xy\)-plane away from the centre. Inside the full sphere, the total electric field at \(P\) is:
\[\mathbf{E}_{\text{upper}} + \mathbf{E}_{\text{lower}} = 0\]

Step 3: Application
By mirror symmetry across the \(xy\)-plane, the component of the electric field parallel to the diameter (in the \(xy\)-plane) due to the upper hemisphere equals the component due to the lower hemisphere: \(E_{\parallel, \text{upper}} = E_{\parallel, \text{lower}}\).
Since their sum must be zero, \(2E_{\parallel, \text{upper}} = 0 \implies E_{\parallel, \text{upper}} = 0\).
However, the vertical components (perpendicular to the diameter) from the upper hemisphere all point away from the positively charged surface (in the \(-z\) direction), so they add up to a non-zero resultant perpendicular to the diameter.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the electric field at a point on a diameter away from the centre is directed perpendicular to the diameter.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
मान लीजिए एक एकसमान रूप से धनावेशित अर्धगोलीय कोश विषुवतीय तल (\(z \ge 0\)) के ऊपर स्थित है, जिसका वृत्ताकार आधार \(xy\)-तल में है। एक पूर्ण एकसमान रूप से आवेशित गोलीय कोश के भीतर प्रत्येक बिंदु पर नेट वैद्युत क्षेत्र शून्य होता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
मान लीजिए एक पूर्ण गोलीय कोश ऊपरी अर्धगोले (\(z \ge 0\)) और निचले अर्धगोले (\(z \le 0\)) से मिलकर बना है। \(xy\)-तल में केंद्र से दूर किसी व्यास पर स्थित बिंदु \(P\) पर, पूर्ण गोले के भीतर कुल वैद्युत क्षेत्र शून्य होता है:
\[\mathbf{E}_{\text{upper}} + \mathbf{E}_{\text{lower}} = 0\]

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
\(xy\)-तल के सापेक्ष दर्पण सममिति के कारण, ऊपरी अर्धगोले के कारण व्यास के समानांतर वैद्युत क्षेत्र घटक, निचले अर्धगोले के कारण घटक के बराबर होता है: \(E_{\parallel, \text{upper}} = E_{\parallel, \text{lower}}\)।
चूँकि इनका योग शून्य होना चाहिए, अतः \(2E_{\parallel, \text{upper}} = 0 \implies E_{\parallel, \text{upper}} = 0\)।
परंतु ऊपरी अर्धगोले के कारण ऊर्ध्वाधर घटक (व्यास के लंबवत) सभी धनावेशित पृष्ठ से दूर (\(-z\) दिशा में) होते हैं, इसलिए वे जुड़कर व्यास के लंबवत एक अशून्य परिणामी क्षेत्र बनाते हैं।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः केंद्र से दूर किसी व्यास पर स्थित बिंदु पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र व्यास के लंबवत दिष्ट होता है।

answer.text: at an angle tilted towards the diameter
at an angle tilted away from the diameter.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQII_Q08 - Zero net electric flux over a closed surface

questiontext.text:
If \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\) over a surface, then

यदि किसी पृष्ठ पर \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\) है, तो

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Gauss's law, the net electric flux through a closed surface \(S\) is \(\Phi_E = \oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
If \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\), it means that the net charge enclosed within the surface is zero (\(q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0\)). This can happen either when there are no charges inside, or when equal and opposite charges (such as an electric dipole) are enclosed inside the surface. Therefore, charges may still be present inside, and the electric field on or inside the surface need not be zero or uniform.

Step 3: Application
Net electric flux represents the difference between the number of electric field lines leaving the closed surface and the number of electric field lines entering it. Since the net flux is zero, the number of flux lines entering the surface must be equal to the number of flux lines leaving it.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Thus, \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\) implies that the number of flux lines entering the surface must be equal to the number of flux lines leaving it.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
गॉस के नियम के अनुसार, किसी बंद पृष्ठ \(S\) से गुजरने वाला नेट वैद्युत फ्लक्स \(\Phi_E = \oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\) होता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
यदि \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\) है, तो इसका अर्थ है कि पृष्ठ के भीतर परिबद्ध नेट आवेश शून्य (\(q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0\)) है। यह तब भी संभव है जब पृष्ठ के भीतर कोई आवेश न हो, अथवा जब पृष्ठ के भीतर समान तथा विपरीत आवेश (जैसे वैद्युत द्विध्रुव) परिबद्ध हों। अतः पृष्ठ के भीतर आवेश उपस्थित हो सकते हैं और पृष्ठ पर या भीतर वैद्युत क्षेत्र का शून्य या एकसमान होना आवश्यक नहीं है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
नेट वैद्युत फ्लक्स बंद पृष्ठ से बाहर निकलने वाली तथा भीतर प्रवेश करने वाली वैद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाओं की संख्या के अंतर को दर्शाता है। चूँकि नेट फ्लक्स शून्य है, इसलिए पृष्ठ में प्रवेश करने वाली फ्लक्स रेखाओं की संख्या पृष्ठ से बाहर निकलने वाली फ्लक्स रेखाओं की संख्या के बराबर होनी चाहिए।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\) से यह निष्कर्ष निकलता है कि पृष्ठ में प्रवेश करने वाली फ्लक्स रेखाओं की संख्या पृष्ठ से बाहर निकलने वाली फ्लक्स रेखाओं की संख्या के बराबर होनी चाहिए।

answer.text: the electric field inside the surface and on it is zero.
the electric field inside the surface is necessarily uniform.
the number of flux lines entering the surface must be equal to the number of flux lines leaving it.
all charges must necessarily be outside the surface.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQII_Q09 - Continuity and discontinuity of electric field

questiontext.text:
The Electric field at a point is

किसी बिंदु पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The electric field \(\mathbf{E}\) at any point in space is determined by the spatial distribution of charges according to Coulomb's law and Gauss's law.

Step 2: Evaluation
1. In a charge-free region (where there is no charge at a point), the electric field varies smoothly from point to point, so it is continuous.
2. If there is a charge at that point—whether positive or negative—the electric field exhibits a discontinuity (for example, the field diverges at a point charge or jumps by \(\sigma/\varepsilon_0\) across a charged surface).

Step 3: Application
Thus, the electric field is not always continuous, nor is discontinuity restricted only to negative charges. It is continuous if there is no charge at that point, and discontinuous if there is a charge (positive or negative) at that point.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the electric field at a point is continuous if there is no charge at that point, and discontinuous if there is a charge at that point.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
आकाश में किसी भी बिंदु पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र \(\mathbf{E}\) कूलॉम के नियम तथा गॉस के नियम के अनुसार आवेशों के स्थानिक वितरण द्वारा निर्धारित होता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
1. आवेश-रहित क्षेत्र में (जहाँ किसी बिंदु पर कोई आवेश न हो), वैद्युत क्षेत्र एक बिंदु से दूसरे बिंदु तक सुगमता से बदलता है, अतः वह सतत होता है।
2. यदि उस बिंदु पर कोई आवेश उपस्थित हो—चाहे वह धनात्मक हो या ऋणात्मक—तो वैद्युत क्षेत्र में असततता उत्पन्न होती है (उदाहरण के लिए, बिंदु आवेश पर क्षेत्र अनंत हो जाता है या आवेशित पृष्ठ के आर-पार क्षेत्र में \(\sigma/\varepsilon_0\) का अंतर आ जाता है)।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
इस प्रकार, वैद्युत क्षेत्र सदैव सतत नहीं होता है और न ही इसकी असततता केवल ऋणात्मक आवेश तक सीमित है। यह उस बिंदु पर आवेश न होने पर सतत होता है और आवेश (धनात्मक या ऋणात्मक) होने पर असतत होता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः किसी बिंदु पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र सतत होता है यदि उस बिंदु पर कोई आवेश न हो, तथा असतत होता है यदि उस बिंदु पर कोई आवेश हो।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQII_Q10 - Gauss law with only one type of charge

questiontext.text:
If there were only one type of charge in the universe, then

यदि ब्रह्मांड में केवल एक ही प्रकार का आवेश होता, तो

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Gauss's law states that the electric flux through any closed surface \(S\) is \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\), which arises directly from the inverse-square nature of Coulomb's law.

Step 2: Evaluation
Even if there were only one type of charge in the universe, the inverse-square law of electrostatics would still hold, and the surface integral \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S}\) would remain well-defined.
- If a charge is located outside the closed surface \(S\), the enclosed charge is zero, so \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\).
- If charges of magnitude \(q\) are inside the closed surface \(S\), then \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\).

Step 3: Application
It is incorrect to say that the flux would be non-zero on every surface, because a surface enclosing no charge still has zero net flux.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\) if the charge is outside the surface, and \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\) if charges of magnitude \(q\) are inside the surface.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
गॉस का नियम बताता है कि किसी भी बंद पृष्ठ \(S\) से गुजरने वाला वैद्युत फ्लक्स \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\) होता है, जो सीधे कूलॉम के व्युत्क्रम-वर्ग नियम से प्राप्त होता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
यदि ब्रह्मांड में केवल एक ही प्रकार का आवेश होता, तब भी स्थिरवैद्युतिकी का व्युत्क्रम-वर्ग नियम लागू रहता और पृष्ठ समाकलन \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S}\) पूर्णतः परिभाषित होता।
- यदि आवेश बंद पृष्ठ \(S\) के बाहर स्थित है, तो परिबद्ध आवेश शून्य होगा, अतः \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\)।
- यदि \(q\) परिमाण के आवेश बंद पृष्ठ \(S\) के भीतर स्थित हैं, तो \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\)।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
यह कहना गलत है कि किसी भी पृष्ठ पर फ्लक्स अशून्य होगा, क्योंकि जिस पृष्ठ के भीतर कोई आवेश नहीं है, उस पर नेट फ्लक्स शून्य ही रहेगा।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः यदि आवेश पृष्ठ के बाहर हो तो \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\) होगा, तथा यदि \(q\) परिमाण के आवेश पृष्ठ के भीतर हों तो \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\) होगा।

answer.text: \(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0\) if the charge is outside the surface.
\(\oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\) if charges of magnitude \(q\) were inside the surface.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQII_Q11 - Electric field outside a region with zero total charge

questiontext.text:
Consider a region inside which there are various types of charges but the total charge is zero. At points outside the region

एक ऐसे क्षेत्र पर विचार कीजिए जिसके भीतर विभिन्न प्रकार के आवेश हैं, परंतु कुल आवेश शून्य है। इस क्षेत्र के बाहर के बिंदुओं पर

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For a charge distribution whose net total charge (monopole moment) is zero, the electric potential and electric field at large distances \(r\) outside the region are governed by the multipole expansion (dipole, quadrupole, and higher-order moments).

Step 2: Evaluation
1. Even though the total charge is zero, the electric field outside is not necessarily zero (for instance, an electric dipole has zero net charge but produces a non-zero electric field).
2. The field is not due to the dipole moment *only*, because quadrupole and higher multipole moments can also contribute.
3. For large \(r\) (far from the region), the dipole term dominates over higher-order multipole terms, so the dominant electric field varies as \(\frac{1}{r^3}\).
4. Because the electrostatic field is conservative (\(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = 0\)), the work done in moving a charged particle along any closed path away from the region is zero.

Step 3: Application
Combining these facts, the dominant electric field at large \(r\) is proportional to \(\frac{1}{r^3}\), and the work done along a closed path outside the region is zero.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, at points outside the region, the dominant electric field is \(\propto \frac{1}{r^3}\) for large \(r\), and the work done to move a charged particle along a closed path away from the region will be zero.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
एक ऐसे आवेश वितरण के लिए जिसका कुल नेट आवेश (एकध्रुव आघूर्ण) शून्य है, क्षेत्र के बाहर बड़ी दूरी \(r\) पर वैद्युत विभव तथा वैद्युत क्षेत्र बहुध्रुव प्रसार (द्विध्रुव, चतुर्ध्रुव तथा उच्चतर आघूर्ण) द्वारा निर्धारित होते हैं।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
1. यद्यपि कुल आवेश शून्य है, फिर भी बाहर वैद्युत क्षेत्र का शून्य होना आवश्यक नहीं है (उदाहरण के लिए, एक वैद्युत द्विध्रुव का नेट आवेश शून्य होता है, परंतु यह अशून्य वैद्युत क्षेत्र उत्पन्न करता है)।
2. वैद्युत क्षेत्र *केवल* द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण के कारण ही नहीं होता, क्योंकि इसमें चतुर्ध्रुव तथा उच्चतर बहुध्रुव आघूर्णों का भी योगदान हो सकता है।
3. बड़े \(r\) के लिए (क्षेत्र से दूर), उच्चतर बहुध्रुव पदों की तुलना में द्विध्रुव पद प्रभावी होता है, अतः प्रभावी वैद्युत क्षेत्र \(\frac{1}{r^3}\) के अनुक्रमानुपाती होता है।
4. चूँकि स्थिरवैद्युत क्षेत्र संरक्षी होता है (\(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = 0\)), इसलिए क्षेत्र से दूर किसी भी बंद पथ के अनुदिश एक आवेशित कण को ले जाने में किया गया कार्य शून्य होता है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
इन तथ्यों के आधार पर, बड़े \(r\) के लिए प्रभावी वैद्युत क्षेत्र \(\frac{1}{r^3}\) के अनुक्रमानुपाती होता है तथा क्षेत्र के बाहर बंद पथ पर किया गया कार्य शून्य होता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः क्षेत्र के बाहर के बिंदुओं पर, बड़े \(r\) के लिए प्रभावी वैद्युत क्षेत्र \(\propto \frac{1}{r^3}\) होता है तथा क्षेत्र से दूर किसी बंद पथ पर आवेशित कण को ले जाने में किया गया कार्य शून्य होगा।

answer.text: the electric field is due to the dipole moment of the charge distribution only.
the dominant electric field is \(\propto \frac{1}{r^3}\), for large \(r\), where \(r\) is the distance from a origin in this region.
the work done to move a charged particle along a closed path, away from the region, will be zero.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQII_Q12 - Flux and field due to charges inside and outside a Gaussian sphere

questiontext.text:
Refer to the arrangement of charges in Fig. 1.6 and a Gaussian surface of radius \(R\) with \(Q\) at the centre. Then

चित्र 1.6 में आवेशों की व्यवस्था तथा केंद्र पर \(Q\) के साथ \(R\) त्रिज्या के एक गॉसीय पृष्ठ को देखिए। तब

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
A spherical Gaussian surface of radius \(R\) has a charge \(Q\) at its centre. A second charge \(-2Q\) is located inside the sphere at a distance \(R/2\) below the centre. A third charge \(5Q\) is located outside the Gaussian surface at a distance \(R\) from its outer surface (i.e., \(2R\) from the centre).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Outward electric flux is taken as positive, and inward electric flux is taken as negative.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By Gauss's law, the total electric flux through the closed spherical surface is:
\[\Phi = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. Total charge enclosed within the Gaussian sphere:
\[q_{\text{enclosed}} = Q + (-2Q) = -Q\]
Therefore, the total flux through the surface of the sphere is:
\[\Phi = \frac{-Q}{\varepsilon_0}\]
2. Because \(-2Q\) is not at the centre and \(5Q\) is outside, the charge distribution is not spherically symmetric about the centre. Hence, the electric field on the surface is not uniform and is not equal to \(\frac{-Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^2}\) everywhere.
3. Since \(5Q\) lies outside the closed Gaussian surface, all field lines from \(5Q\) that enter the sphere also leave it; thus, the net flux through the sphere due to \(5Q\) is zero.
4. Because \(-2Q\) is located off-centre (at distance \(R/2\) from the centre), its distance to different points on the spherical surface varies between \(R/2\) and \(3R/2\). Therefore, the field on the surface due to \(-2Q\) is not the same everywhere.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Hence, the total flux through the surface of the sphere is \(\frac{-Q}{\varepsilon_0}\), and the flux through the surface of the sphere due to \(5Q\) is zero.

चरण 1: दिए गए आँकड़े और शर्तें
\(R\) त्रिज्या के एक गोलीय गॉसीय पृष्ठ के केंद्र पर एक आवेश \(Q\) स्थित है। एक दूसरा आवेश \(-2Q\) गोले के भीतर केंद्र से \(R/2\) दूरी पर नीचे स्थित है। एक तीसरा आवेश \(5Q\) गॉसीय पृष्ठ के बाहर उसकी बाहरी सतह से \(R\) दूरी पर (अर्थात केंद्र से \(2R\) दूरी पर) स्थित है।

चरण 2: मान्यताएँ और चिह्न परिपाटी
बाहर की ओर जाने वाले वैद्युत फ्लक्स को धनात्मक तथा भीतर आने वाले वैद्युत फ्लक्स को ऋणात्मक माना गया है।

चरण 3: संबंधित सूत्र और सिद्धांत
गॉस के नियम से, बंद गोलीय पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाला कुल वैद्युत फ्लक्स है:
\[\Phi = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\]

चरण 4: चरणबद्ध हल
1. गॉसीय गोले के भीतर परिबद्ध कुल आवेश:
\[q_{\text{enclosed}} = Q + (-2Q) = -Q\]
अतः गोले के पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाला कुल फ्लक्स:
\[\Phi = \frac{-Q}{\varepsilon_0}\]
2. चूँकि \(-2Q\) केंद्र पर नहीं है और \(5Q\) बाहर है, इसलिए आवेश वितरण केंद्र के परितः गोलीय रूप से सममित नहीं है। अतः पृष्ठ पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र एकसमान नहीं है और सर्वत्र \(\frac{-Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^2}\) के बराबर नहीं है।
3. चूँकि \(5Q\) बंद गॉसीय पृष्ठ के बाहर स्थित है, इसलिए \(5Q\) से निकलने वाली जितनी क्षेत्र रेखाएँ गोले में प्रवेश करती हैं, उतनी ही बाहर निकल जाती हैं; अतः \(5Q\) के कारण गोले से गुजरने वाला नेट फ्लक्स शून्य है।
4. चूँकि \(-2Q\) केंद्र से हटकर (केंद्र से \(R/2\) दूरी पर) स्थित है, इसलिए गोलीय पृष्ठ के विभिन्न बिंदुओं से इसकी दूरी \(R/2\) से \(3R/2\) के बीच बदलती है। अतः \(-2Q\) के कारण पृष्ठ पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र सर्वत्र समान नहीं है।

चरण 5: जाँच और अंतिम उत्तर
अतः गोले के पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाला कुल फ्लक्स \(\frac{-Q}{\varepsilon_0}\) है, तथा \(5Q\) के कारण गोले के पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाला फ्लक्स शून्य है।

answer.text: total flux through the surface of the sphere is \(\frac{-Q}{\varepsilon_0}\).
field on the surface of the sphere is \(\frac{-Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^2}\).
flux through the surface of sphere due to \(5Q\) is zero.
field on the surface of sphere due to \(-2Q\) is same everywhere.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH01_MCQII_Q13 - Equilibrium and SHM of a test charge at the centre of a charged ring

questiontext.text:
A positive charge \(Q\) is uniformly distributed along a circular ring of radius \(R\). A small test charge \(q\) is placed at the centre of the ring (Fig. 1.7). Then

एक धनात्मक आवेश \(Q\), \(R\) त्रिज्या के एक वृत्ताकार वलय के अनुदिश एकसमान रूप से वितरित है। वलय के केंद्र पर एक छोटा परीक्षण आवेश \(q\) रखा गया है (चित्र 1.7)। तब

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
A circular ring of radius \(R\) carries a uniformly distributed positive charge \(Q\). A small test charge \(q\) is placed at the centre of the ring.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Displacement in the plane of the ring is radial, while displacement along the axis of the ring is denoted by \(z\) (with \(|z| \ll R\) for small displacements).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. The electric field at an axial distance \(z\) from the centre of a uniformly charged ring of radius \(R\) and charge \(Q\) is:
\[E_z = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Qz}{(R^2 + z^2)^{3/2}}\]
directed away from the centre along the axis.
2. The force on test charge \(q\) is \(\mathbf{F} = q\mathbf{E}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. Displacement in the plane of the ring for \(q > 0\): When \(q > 0\) is displaced slightly from the centre towards one side of the ring, it comes closer to that positively charged arc of the ring. The repulsive force from the nearer part of the ring becomes stronger than that from the farther part, pushing \(q\) back towards the centre. Hence, \(q > 0\) is in stable equilibrium in the plane of the ring.
2. Displacement in the plane of the ring for \(q < 0\): When \(q < 0\) is displaced towards one side in the plane of the ring, the attractive force from the nearer part of the positively charged ring exceeds that from the farther part. Thus, it experiences a net force away from the centre and continues moving until it hits the ring.
3. Small displacement along the axis for \(q < 0\): For \(|z| \ll R\), the axial electric field approximates to:
\[E_z \approx \frac{Qz}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^3}\]
For \(q < 0\), the force is:
\[F_z = qE_z = -\frac{|q|Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^3} z\]
Since \(F_z \propto -z\) is a restoring force directed towards the centre, the charge \(q < 0\) performs simple harmonic motion (SHM) for small displacements along the axis.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Therefore: for \(q > 0\) displaced in the plane, it is pushed back towards the centre (stable equilibrium in the plane); for \(q < 0\) displaced in the plane, it continues moving till it hits the ring; and for \(q < 0\), it performs SHM for small displacements along the axis.

चरण 1: दिए गए आँकड़े और शर्तें
\(R\) त्रिज्या के एक वृत्ताकार वलय पर धनात्मक आवेश \(Q\) एकसमान रूप से वितरित है। वलय के केंद्र पर एक छोटा परीक्षण आवेश \(q\) रखा गया है।

चरण 2: मान्यताएँ और चिह्न परिपाटी
वलय के तल में विस्थापन त्रिज्यीय है, जबकि वलय के अक्ष के अनुदिश विस्थापन को \(z\) से दर्शाया गया है (छोटे विस्थापन के लिए \(|z| \ll R\))।

चरण 3: संबंधित सूत्र और सिद्धांत
1. \(R\) त्रिज्या तथा \(Q\) आवेश वाले एकसमान रूप से आवेशित वलय के केंद्र से अक्षीय दूरी \(z\) पर वैद्युत क्षेत्र है:
\[E_z = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Qz}{(R^2 + z^2)^{3/2}}\]
जो अक्ष के अनुदिश केंद्र से दूर की ओर दिष्ट होता है।
2. परीक्षण आवेश \(q\) पर लगने वाला बल \(\mathbf{F} = q\mathbf{E}\) होता है।

चरण 4: चरणबद्ध हल
1. \(q > 0\) के लिए वलय के तल में विस्थापन: जब \(q > 0\) को केंद्र से वलय के एक ओर थोड़ा विस्थापित किया जाता है, तो वह वलय के उस धनावेशित भाग के निकट आ जाता है। वलय के निकट वाले भाग से लगने वाला प्रतिकर्षण बल दूर वाले भाग से लगने वाले बल से अधिक हो जाता है, जिससे \(q\) वापस केंद्र की ओर धकेल दिया जाता है। अतः \(q > 0\) वलय के तल में स्थायी संतुलन में है।
2. \(q < 0\) के लिए वलय के तल में विस्थापन: जब \(q < 0\) को वलय के तल में एक ओर विस्थापित किया जाता है, तो धनावेशित वलय के निकट वाले भाग का आकर्षण बल दूर वाले भाग से अधिक हो जाता है। अतः उस पर केंद्र से दूर की ओर नेट बल लगता है और वह वलय से टकराने तक चलता रहता है।
3. \(q < 0\) के लिए अक्ष के अनुदिश छोटा विस्थापन: \(|z| \ll R\) के लिए, अक्षीय वैद्युत क्षेत्र लगभग होता है:
\[E_z \approx \frac{Qz}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^3}\]
\(q < 0\) के लिए बल है:
\[F_z = qE_z = -\frac{|q|Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^3} z\]
चूँकि \(F_z \propto -z\) केंद्र की ओर दिष्ट एक प्रत्यानयन बल है, इसलिए आवेश \(q < 0\) अक्ष के अनुदिश छोटे विस्थापन के लिए सरल आवर्त गति (SHM) करेगा।

चरण 5: जाँच और अंतिम उत्तर
अतः \(q > 0\) को तल में विस्थापित करने पर यह वापस केंद्र की ओर धकेल दिया जाएगा (तल में स्थायी संतुलन); \(q < 0\) को तल में विस्थापित करने पर यह वलय से टकराने तक चलता रहेगा; तथा \(q < 0\) अक्ष के अनुदिश छोटे विस्थापन के लिए सरल आवर्त गति करेगा।

answer.text: If \(q > 0\) and is displaced away from the centre in the plane of the ring, it will be pushed back towards the centre.
If \(q < 0\) and is displaced away from the centre in the plane of the ring, it will never return to the centre and will continue moving till it hits the ring.
If \(q < 0\), it will perform SHM for small displacement along the axis.
\(q\) at the centre of the ring is in an unstable equilibrium within the plane of the ring for \(q > 0\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQI_Q2_1 - Charge on capacitor in steady state circuit

questiontext.text: A capacitor of \(4\ \mu\mathrm{F}\) is connected as shown in the circuit (Fig. 2.1). The internal resistance of the battery is \(0.5\ \Omega\). The amount of charge on the capacitor plates will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Capacitance of the capacitor, \(C = 4\ \mu\mathrm{F}\).
Emf of the battery, \(E = 2.5\ \mathrm{V}\).
Internal resistance of the battery, \(r = 0.5\ \Omega\).
Resistance in series with the capacitor in the top branch, \(R_{1} = 10\ \Omega\).
External resistance in the bottom parallel branch, \(R_{2} = 2\ \Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The circuit is assumed to be in DC steady state, meaning the capacitor is fully charged and acts as an open circuit, so zero current flows through the capacitor branch.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Steady-state current in a closed loop with internal resistance: \(I = \frac{E}{R_{2} + r}\).
2. Terminal potential difference across the battery and parallel branch: \(V = I R_{2}\).
3. Charge stored on a capacitor: \(Q = C V\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Since no current flows through the \(10\ \Omega\) resistor in steady state, the current \(I\) flows only through the loop containing the \(2.5\ \mathrm{V}\) battery and the \(2\ \Omega\) resistor:
\[I = \frac{2.5\ \mathrm{V}}{2\ \Omega + 0.5\ \Omega} = \frac{2.5}{2.5} = 1\ \mathrm{A}\]
The potential difference across the \(2\ \Omega\) resistor (and hence across the parallel capacitor branch) is:
\[V = I R_{2} = 1\ \mathrm{A} \times 2\ \Omega = 2\ \mathrm{V}\]
Because there is no current through the \(10\ \Omega\) resistor, there is no potential drop across it, so the entire \(2\ \mathrm{V}\) appears across the \(4\ \mu\mathrm{F}\) capacitor.
The charge on the capacitor plates is:
\[Q = C V = 4\ \mu\mathrm{F} \times 2\ \mathrm{V} = 8\ \mu\mathrm{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The terminal voltage \(2\ \mathrm{V}\) is less than the emf \(2.5\ \mathrm{V}\), which is physically consistent with a potential drop \(I r = 0.5\ \mathrm{V}\) across the internal resistance. The units \(\mu\mathrm{F} \cdot \mathrm{V} = \mu\mathrm{C}\) are consistent.
Final Answer: \(8\ \mu\mathrm{C}\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQI_Q2_2 - Electric potential energy of released positive charge

questiontext.text: A positively charged particle is released from rest in a uniform electric field. The electric potential energy of the charge

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A charge \(q\) placed in an electric field \(\mathbf{E}\) experiences an electrostatic force \(\mathbf{F} = q\mathbf{E}\). Also, the electric field always points in the direction of decreasing electrostatic potential.

Step 2: Evaluation
For a positively charged particle (\(q > 0\)), the force \(\mathbf{F} = q\mathbf{E}\) acts in the same direction as the electric field \(\mathbf{E}\). Since the particle is released from rest, it accelerates and moves along the direction of the electric field.

Step 3: Application
As the positive charge moves along the electric field, the electric field does positive work on the charge, converting electric potential energy into kinetic energy. Equivalently, since the potential \(V\) decreases along the electric field and \(U = qV\) with \(q > 0\), the electric potential energy \(U\) decreases.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The electric potential energy of the charge decreases because the charge moves along the electric field.

answer.text: remains a constant because the electric field is uniform.
increases because the charge moves along the electric field.
decreases because the charge moves along the electric field.
decreases because the charge moves opposite to the electric field.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQI_Q2_3 - Work done moving charge between equipotential lines

questiontext.text: Figure 2.2 shows some equipotential lines distributed in space. A charged object is moved from point A to point B.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Three different spatial distributions of equipotential lines are shown, with potentials marked at \(10\ \mathrm{V}\), \(20\ \mathrm{V}\), \(30\ \mathrm{V}\), \(40\ \mathrm{V}\), and \(50\ \mathrm{V}\). In every distribution, point A lies on the \(20\ \mathrm{V}\) equipotential line and point B lies on the \(40\ \mathrm{V}\) equipotential line.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Let \(q\) be the charge of the object moved from point A to point B. The electrostatic field is conservative.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The work done in moving a charge \(q\) from potential \(V_{A}\) to potential \(V_{B}\) in an electrostatic field is:
\[W_{AB} = q (V_{B} - V_{A})\]
Because the electrostatic force is conservative, the work done depends only on the initial and final potentials and is independent of the path or the spacing of intermediate equipotential lines.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For all three equipotential distributions:
\[V_{A} = 20\ \mathrm{V}, \quad V_{B} = 40\ \mathrm{V}\]
Therefore, the potential difference is:
\[\Delta V = V_{B} - V_{A} = 40\ \mathrm{V} - 20\ \mathrm{V} = 20\ \mathrm{V}\]
Hence, the work done in each case is \(W_{AB} = 20q\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since both the charge \(q\) and the potential difference \(\Delta V = 20\ \mathrm{V}\) are identical in all three cases, the work done is identical in all three distributions.
Final Answer: The work done is the same in all three cases.

answer.text: The work done in Fig. (i) is the greatest.
The work done in Fig. (ii) is least.
The work done is the same in Fig. (i), Fig. (ii) and Fig. (iii).
The work done in Fig. (iii) is greater than Fig. (ii) but equal to that in Fig. (i).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQI_Q2_4 - Electric field and potential inside conducting sphere

questiontext.text:
The electrostatic potential on the surface of a charged conducting sphere is \(100\ \mathrm{V}\). Two statements are made in this regard:

\(S_{1}\): At any point inside the sphere, electric intensity is zero.

\(S_{2}\): At any point inside the sphere, the electrostatic potential is \(100\ \mathrm{V}\).

Which of the following is a correct statement?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field inside the volume of a conductor is zero everywhere. Furthermore, electric field is related to electrostatic potential by \(E = -\frac{dV}{dr}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
Since the electric intensity inside the charged conducting sphere is zero everywhere (\(E = 0\)), the first statement \(S_{1}\) is true. Because \(E = -\frac{dV}{dr} = 0\), the electrostatic potential \(V\) must remain constant throughout the interior of the sphere.

Step 3: Application
Since the potential is continuous across the surface of the sphere and equals \(100\ \mathrm{V}\) on the surface, the constant potential at every point inside the sphere is also \(100\ \mathrm{V}\). Therefore, the second statement \(S_{2}\) is also true, and it is a direct consequence of the electric intensity being zero inside the sphere.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
\(S_{1}\) is true, \(S_{2}\) is also true, and \(S_{1}\) is the cause of \(S_{2}\).

answer.text: \(S_{1}\) is true, \(S_{2}\) is also true and \(S_{1}\) is the cause of \(S_{2}\).
\(S_{1}\) is true, \(S_{2}\) is also true but the statements are independent.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQI_Q2_5 - Equipotentials far from non-zero net charge

questiontext.text: Equipotentials at a great distance from a collection of charges whose total sum is not zero are approximately

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
At distances \(r\) much larger than the spatial extent of a localized charge distribution, the monopole term dominates the multipole expansion of the electrostatic potential if the net charge \(Q = \sum q_{i} \neq 0\).

Step 2: Evaluation
Viewed from a great distance, the entire collection of charges acts approximately as a single point charge \(Q\) located at the origin. The potential at distance \(r\) is given by \(V(r) \approx \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}}\frac{Q}{r}\).

Step 3: Application
An equipotential surface satisfies \(V = \text{constant}\), which corresponds to \(r = \text{constant}\). The locus of points at a constant distance \(r\) from a point is a sphere.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Equipotentials at a great distance from a collection of charges with non-zero total charge are approximately spheres.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQI_Q2_6 - Effective dielectric constant of series dielectric blocks

questiontext.text: A parallel plate capacitor is made of two dielectric blocks in series. One of the blocks has thickness \(d_{1}\) and dielectric constant \(k_{1}\) and the other has thickness \(d_{2}\) and dielectric constant \(k_{2}\) as shown in Fig. 2.3. This arrangement can be thought as a dielectric slab of thickness \(d (= d_{1} + d_{2})\) and effective dielectric constant \(k\). The \(k\) is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
A parallel plate capacitor of plate area \(A\) is filled with two dielectric slabs in series: the first has thickness \(d_{1}\) and dielectric constant \(k_{1}\), and the second has thickness \(d_{2}\) and dielectric constant \(k_{2}\). The total plate separation is \(d = d_{1} + d_{2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Fringing effects at the edges are neglected, so the electric field is uniform within each dielectric slab and perpendicular to the plates.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor filled with a dielectric of constant \(k\), area \(A\), and thickness \(d\): \(C = \frac{k \varepsilon_{0} A}{d}\).
2. Equivalent capacitance of two capacitors \(C_{1}\) and \(C_{2}\) in series: \(\frac{1}{C_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{1}{C_{1}} + \frac{1}{C_{2}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The individual capacitances of the two dielectric blocks are:
\[C_{1} = \frac{k_{1} \varepsilon_{0} A}{d_{1}}, \quad C_{2} = \frac{k_{2} \varepsilon_{0} A}{d_{2}}\]
Since they are in series, the equivalent capacitance \(C_{\text{eq}} = \frac{k \varepsilon_{0} A}{d_{1} + d_{2}}\) satisfies:
\[\frac{d_{1} + d_{2}}{k \varepsilon_{0} A} = \frac{d_{1}}{k_{1} \varepsilon_{0} A} + \frac{d_{2}}{k_{2} \varepsilon_{0} A}\]
Cancelling \(\frac{1}{\varepsilon_{0} A}\) from both sides:
\[\frac{d_{1} + d_{2}}{k} = \frac{d_{1}}{k_{1}} + \frac{d_{2}}{k_{2}} = \frac{k_{2} d_{1} + k_{1} d_{2}}{k_{1} k_{2}}\]
Solving for \(k\) gives:
\[k = \frac{k_{1} k_{2} (d_{1} + d_{2})}{k_{1} d_{2} + k_{2} d_{1}}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The expression is dimensionless, and for equal thicknesses \(d_{1} = d_{2}\) it reduces to the harmonic mean \(\frac{2 k_{1} k_{2}}{k_{1} + k_{2}}\). (Note: In the printed source text, the denominator is written with swapped subscripts as \(k_{1} d_{1} + k_{2} d_{2}\); the matching series-combination form is \(\frac{k_{1} k_{2} (d_{1} + d_{2})}{(k_{1} d_{1} + k_{2} d_{2})}\).)
Final Answer: \(\frac{k_{1} k_{2} (d_{1} + d_{2})}{(k_{1} d_{1} + k_{2} d_{2})}\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQII_Q2_7 - Equipotential surfaces for uniform field along z

questiontext.text: Consider a uniform electric field in the \(\hat{\mathbf{z}}\) direction. The potential is a constant

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The electrostatic potential \(V\) and electric field \(\mathbf{E}\) are related by \(dV = -\mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{r}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
For a uniform electric field \(\mathbf{E} = E_{0}\hat{\mathbf{z}}\), we have:
\[dV = -(E_{0}\hat{\mathbf{z}}) \cdot (dx\,\hat{\mathbf{x}} + dy\,\hat{\mathbf{y}} + dz\,\hat{\mathbf{z}}) = -E_{0}\,dz\]
Integrating gives \(V(x, y, z) = -E_{0} z + C\), where \(C\) is a constant.

Step 3: Application
Since \(V\) depends only on \(z\) and is independent of \(x\) and \(y\), the potential is constant for any \(x\) for a given \(z\), for any \(y\) for a given \(z\), and throughout the entire \(x\text{-}y\) plane for a given \(z\). It is not constant in all space because \(V\) varies linearly with \(z\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The potential is a constant for any \(x\) for a given \(z\), for any \(y\) for a given \(z\), and on the \(x\text{-}y\) plane for a given \(z\).

answer.text: on the \(x - y\) plane for a given \(z\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQII_Q2_8 - Properties of equipotential surfaces and field strength

questiontext.text: Equipotential surfaces

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The magnitude of the electric field is related to the spacing between equipotential surfaces by \(E = -\frac{dV}{dr}\). For a fixed potential difference \(\Delta V\) between successive surfaces, the perpendicular spacing \(\Delta r\) is inversely proportional to the electric field strength: \(\Delta r \propto \frac{1}{E}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
Because \(\Delta r \propto \frac{1}{E}\), equipotential surfaces are closer together in regions of strong electric fields than in regions of weak electric fields. They are equally spaced only when the electric field is uniform, not always.

Step 3: Application
On a charged conductor, the surface charge density \(\sigma\) is largest at sharp edges (small radius of curvature), and the electric field just outside the conductor is \(E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_{0}}\). Therefore, \(E\) is large near sharp edges and near regions of large charge densities, making the equipotential surfaces more crowded in these regions.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Equipotential surfaces are closer in regions of large electric fields compared to regions of lower electric fields, more crowded near sharp edges of a conductor, and more crowded near regions of large charge densities.

answer.text: are closer in regions of large electric fields compared to regions of lower electric fields.
will be more crowded near sharp edges of a conductor.
will be more crowded near regions of large charge densities.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQII_Q2_9 - Work done moving charge along an equipotential

questiontext.text: The work done to move a charge along an equipotential from A to B

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The work done in moving a unit positive charge from point A to point B in an electrostatic field is defined by the line integral \(W_{AB} = -\int_{A}^{B} \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = V_{B} - V_{A}\) (and for any charge \(q\), \(W_{AB} = q(V_{B} - V_{A})\)).

Step 2: Evaluation
Along an equipotential surface, the electric potential is constant everywhere, so \(V_{A} = V_{B}\) and \(V_{B} - V_{A} = 0\). Equivalently, the electric field \(\mathbf{E}\) is always perpendicular to the equipotential surface, so \(\mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = 0\) at every point along the path.

Step 3: Application
Thus, the work done must be defined as \(-\int_{A}^{B} \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l}\) (per unit charge) and evaluates to zero along an equipotential surface.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The work done to move a charge along an equipotential from A to B must be defined as \(-\int_{A}^{B} \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l}\) and is zero.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQII_Q2_10 - Electric field and charge in constant potential region

questiontext.text: In a region of constant potential

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The electric field is the negative gradient of the electrostatic potential: \(\mathbf{E} = -\nabla V\). According to Gauss's law, the net electric flux through any closed surface equals \(\frac{q_{\text{in}}}{\varepsilon_{0}}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
If the potential \(V\) is constant throughout a region, all spatial derivatives of \(V\) vanish, so the electric field \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) everywhere in that region.

Step 3: Application
Because \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) everywhere inside the region, the electric flux through any closed Gaussian surface drawn within the region is zero. By Gauss's law, this implies there can be no net charge inside the region. Furthermore, if the region is enclosed by a conductor (electrostatic shielding), placing a charge outside induces surface charges that keep the interior field zero, so the electric field inside does not necessarily change.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
In a region of constant potential, the electric field is zero and there can be no charge inside the region.

answer.text: there can be no charge inside the region.
the electric field shall necessarily change if a charge is placed outside the region.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQII_Q2_11 - Charge redistribution between two capacitors in circuit

questiontext.text:
In the circuit shown in Fig. 2.4, initially key \(K_{1}\) is closed and key \(K_{2}\) is open. Then \(K_{1}\) is opened and \(K_{2}\) is closed (order is important). [Take \(Q_{1}'\) and \(Q_{2}'\) as charges on \(C_{1}\) and \(C_{2}\) and \(V_{1}\) and \(V_{2}\) as voltage respectively.]

Then

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Capacitors \(C_{1}\) and \(C_{2}\) are connected in a circuit with a battery of emf \(E\) and keys \(K_{1}\) and \(K_{2}\). Initially \(K_{1}\) is closed and \(K_{2}\) is open. Later \(K_{1}\) is opened and \(K_{2}\) is closed. After redistribution, the charges on \(C_{1}\) and \(C_{2}\) are \(Q_{1}'\) and \(Q_{2}'\) and their voltages are \(V_{1}\) and \(V_{2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Both capacitors are initially uncharged, and the battery and connecting wires have negligible resistance.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Charge on a capacitor: \(Q = C V\).
2. Conservation of electric charge on an isolated system of plates.
3. Parallel capacitors in electrostatic equilibrium have equal potential differences.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
When \(K_{1}\) is closed and \(K_{2}\) is open, capacitor \(C_{1}\) is charged to the battery emf \(E\), acquiring an initial charge:
\[Q = C_{1} E\]
When \(K_{1}\) is opened, the battery is disconnected, and when \(K_{2}\) is closed, \(C_{1}\) and \(C_{2}\) are connected in parallel. Charge redistributes until both capacitors reach a common potential difference:
\[V_{1} = V_{2}\]
By conservation of charge on the isolated plates:
\[Q_{1}' + Q_{2}' = Q\]
Substituting \(Q_{1}' = C_{1} V_{1}\), \(Q_{2}' = C_{2} V_{2}\), and \(Q = C_{1} E\) gives:
\[C_{1} V_{1} + C_{2} V_{2} = C_{1} E\]
Note that \(Q_{1}' = Q_{2}'\) holds only in the special case \(C_{1} = C_{2}\), not in general.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The equations \(V_{1} = V_{2}\), \(Q_{1}' + Q_{2}' = Q\), and \(C_{1} V_{1} + C_{2} V_{2} = C_{1} E\) all follow directly from parallel connection and charge conservation.
Final Answer: Charge on \(C_{1}\) gets redistributed such that \(V_{1} = V_{2}\), \(C_{1}V_{1} + C_{2}V_{2} = C_{1}E\), and \(Q_{1}' + Q_{2}' = Q\).

answer.text: charge on \(C_{1}\) gets redistributed such that \(V_{1} = V_{2}\)
charge on \(C_{1}\) gets redistributed such that \(Q_{1}' = Q_{2}'\)
charge on \(C_{1}\) gets redistributed such that \(C_{1}V_{1} + C_{2}V_{2} = C_{1}E\)
charge on \(C_{1}\) gets redistributed such that \(Q_{1}' + Q_{2}' = Q\)

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQII_Q2_12 - Charge distribution on conductor at non-zero potential

questiontext.text: If a conductor has a potential \(V \neq 0\) and there are no charges anywhere else outside, then

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field inside the conducting material (the body of the conductor) is zero. By Gauss's law, the net charge enclosed within any region where \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) is zero.

Step 2: Evaluation
Since the conductor has a non-zero potential \(V \neq 0\) (with reference potential zero at infinity) and there are no charges anywhere outside, the conductor itself must possess charges—either on its outer surface or inside a cavity within itself.

Step 3: Application
Because \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) throughout the solid conducting material, there cannot be any net charge in the body of the conductor. Any excess charge on an isolated conductor resides on its surface (or on the inner surface if a charge is placed inside a cavity).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
There must be charges on the surface or inside itself, and there cannot be any charge in the body of the conductor.

answer.text: there must be charges on the surface or inside itself.
there cannot be any charge in the body of the conductor.
there must be charges only on the surface.
there must be charges inside the surface.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_PHYSICS_MCQII_Q2_13 - Parallel plate capacitor with key closed or open

questiontext.text:
A parallel plate capacitor is connected to a battery as shown in Fig. 2.5. Consider two situations:

A: Key K is kept closed and plates of capacitors are moved apart using insulating handle.

B: Key K is opened and plates of capacitors are moved apart using insulating handle.

Choose the correct option(s).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance \(C\) is connected to a battery of emf \(E\) via a key \(K\). In situation A, key \(K\) remains closed while the plate separation \(d\) is increased. In situation B, key \(K\) is opened before the plate separation \(d\) is increased.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
An insulating handle is used so no charge leaks through the handle. Edge effects are neglected.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor: \(C = \frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d}\).
2. Charge-voltage relation: \(Q = C V\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
When the plates are moved apart, \(d\) increases, so the capacitance \(C = \frac{\varepsilon_{0} A}{d}\) decreases in both situations.
In situation A (key \(K\) closed), the capacitor stays connected to the battery, so the potential difference \(V = E\) remains constant. Since \(Q = C V\) and \(C\) decreases, the charge \(Q\) changes (decreases).
In situation B (key \(K\) opened), the capacitor is isolated from the battery, so the charge \(Q\) on the plates remains constant. Since \(V = \frac{Q}{C}\) and \(C\) decreases, the potential difference \(V\) changes (increases).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both conclusions follow directly from \(Q = C V\) under constant-\(V\) (battery connected) and constant-\(Q\) (battery disconnected) constraints.
Final Answer: In A: \(V\) remains same and hence \(Q\) changes; in B: \(Q\) remains same and hence \(V\) changes.

answer.text: In A: \(V\) remains same and hence \(Q\) changes.
In B: \(Q\) remains same and hence \(V\) changes.

name.text: NEETUG_PHYSICS_MCQI_CH02_Q01 - Charge on capacitor plates in steady state circuit

questiontext.text:
2.1 A capacitor of \(4\,\mu\mathrm{F}\) is connected as shown in the circuit (Fig. 2.1). The internal resistance of the battery is \(0.5\,\Omega\). The amount of charge on the capacitor plates will be

Fig. 2.1

২.১ একটি \(4\,\mu\mathrm{F}\) ধারককে চিত্রে (চিত্র ২.১) প্রদর্শিত বর্তনী অনুযায়ী সংযুক্ত করা হয়েছে। ব্যাটারির অভ্যন্তরীণ রোধ \(0.5\,\Omega\)। ধারকের পাতগুলোতে আধানের পরিমাণ হবে

চিত্র ২.১

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Capacitance of the capacitor, \(C = 4\,\mu\mathrm{F}\); EMF of the battery, \(E = 2.5\,\mathrm{V}\); internal resistance of the battery, \(r = 0.5\,\Omega\); resistance in series with the capacitor, \(R_1 = 10\,\Omega\); external resistor connected in parallel with the battery and capacitor branch, \(R_2 = 2\,\Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The circuit has reached steady state with a DC source. In steady state, a fully charged capacitor acts as an open circuit, so zero current flows through the branch containing the capacitor and the \(10\,\Omega\) resistor.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Current in the closed resistive loop: \(I = \frac{E}{R_2 + r}\). Terminal potential difference across the \(2\,\Omega\) resistor (and hence across the capacitor branch): \(V = I R_2\). Charge stored on the capacitor: \(Q = C V\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The steady-state current flowing through the battery and the \(2\,\Omega\) resistor is:
\(I = \frac{2.5\,\mathrm{V}}{2\,\Omega + 0.5\,\Omega} = \frac{2.5}{2.5}\,\mathrm{A} = 1\,\mathrm{A}\).
Since no current flows through the \(10\,\Omega\) resistor, there is no potential drop across it. Therefore, the potential difference across the capacitor equals the potential difference across the \(2\,\Omega\) resistor:
\(V = I R_2 = 1\,\mathrm{A} \times 2\,\Omega = 2\,\mathrm{V}\).
The charge stored on the capacitor plates is:
\(Q = C V = 4\,\mu\mathrm{F} \times 2\,\mathrm{V} = 8\,\mu\mathrm{C}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The terminal voltage \(2\,\mathrm{V}\) is less than the EMF \(2.5\,\mathrm{V}\) because of the \(0.5\,\mathrm{V}\) drop across the internal resistance, which is physically consistent. Thus, the charge on the capacitor plates is \(8\,\mu\mathrm{C}\).

ধাপ ১: প্রদত্ত তথ্য ও শর্তাবলি
ধারকের ধারকত্ব, \(C = 4\,\mu\mathrm{F}\); ব্যাটারির তড়িচ্চালক বল, \(E = 2.5\,\mathrm{V}\); ব্যাটারির অভ্যন্তরীণ রোধ, \(r = 0.5\,\Omega\); ধারকের সাথে শ্রেণি সমবায়ে যুক্ত রোধ, \(R_1 = 10\,\Omega\); ব্যাটারি ও ধারক শাখার সাথে সমান্তরালে যুক্ত বহিস্থ রোধ, \(R_2 = 2\,\Omega\)।

ধাপ ২: অনুমান ও চিহ্ন প্রথা
একমুখী তড়িৎ উৎস (DC) যুক্ত বর্তনীটি স্থির অবস্থায় (steady state) রয়েছে। স্থির অবস্থায় একটি পূর্ণ আহিত ধারক মুক্ত বর্তনীর (open circuit) ন্যায় আচরণ করে, তাই ধারক ও \(10\,\Omega\) রোধযুক্ত শাখায় কোনো তড়িৎ প্রবাহিত হয় না।

ধাপ ৩: প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতি
বদ্ধ রোধীয় লুপে তড়িৎ প্রবাহ: \(I = \frac{E}{R_2 + r}\)। \(2\,\Omega\) রোধের দুই প্রান্তে বিভব পার্থক্য (যা ধারক শাখার বিভব পার্থক্যের সমান): \(V = I R_2\)। ধারকে সঞ্চিত আধান: \(Q = C V\)।

ধাপ ৪: ধাপে ধাপে সমাধান
ব্যাটারি ও \(2\,\Omega\) রোধের মধ্য দিয়ে প্রবাহিত স্থির অবস্থার তড়িৎ প্রবাহ হলো:
\(I = \frac{2.5\,\mathrm{V}}{2\,\Omega + 0.5\,\Omega} = \frac{2.5}{2.5}\,\mathrm{A} = 1\,\mathrm{A}\)।
যেহেতু \(10\,\Omega\) রোধের মধ্য দিয়ে কোনো তড়িৎ প্রবাহিত হয় না, তাই এর দুই প্রান্তে কোনো বিভব পতন ঘটে না। ফলে ধারকের দুই প্রান্তের বিভব পার্থক্য \(2\,\Omega\) রোধের বিভব পার্থক্যের সমান হয়:
\(V = I R_2 = 1\,\mathrm{A} \times 2\,\Omega = 2\,\mathrm{V}\)।
ধারকের পাতগুলোতে সঞ্চিত আধানের পরিমাণ:
\(Q = C V = 4\,\mu\mathrm{F} \times 2\,\mathrm{V} = 8\,\mu\mathrm{C}\)।

ধাপ ৫: যাচাই ও চূড়ান্ত উত্তর
অভ্যন্তরীণ রোধে \(0.5\,\mathrm{V}\) বিভব পতনের কারণে প্রান্তীয় বিভব \(2\,\mathrm{V}\) ব্যাটারির তড়িচ্চালক বল \(2.5\,\mathrm{V}\) অপেক্ষা কম, যা ভৌতভাবে সঙ্গতিপূর্ণ। সুতরাং, ধারকের পাতগুলোতে আধানের পরিমাণ \(8\,\mu\mathrm{C}\)।

name.text: NEETUG_PHYSICS_MCQI_CH02_Q02 - Electric potential energy of positive charge released from rest

questiontext.text:
2.2 A positively charged particle is released from rest in an uniform electric field. The electric potential energy of the charge

২.২ একটি ধনাত্মক আধানযুক্ত কণাকে সুষম তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রে স্থির অবস্থা থেকে ছেড়ে দেওয়া হলো। আধানটির তড়িৎ স্থিতিশক্তি

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A positive charge \(q > 0\) placed in a uniform electric field \(\mathbf{E}\) experiences an electrostatic force \(\mathbf{F} = q\mathbf{E}\) in the same direction as \(\mathbf{E}\). Also, electrostatic potential \(V\) always decreases in the direction of the electric field.

Step 2: Evaluation
Since the particle is released from rest, it accelerates and moves in the direction of the net force, which is along the electric field \(\mathbf{E}\). As it moves along \(\mathbf{E}\), the electrostatic field does positive work on the charge, increasing its kinetic energy.

Step 3: Application
By conservation of mechanical energy in an electrostatic field, an increase in kinetic energy corresponds to an equal decrease in electric potential energy \(U = qV\) (equivalently, since \(V\) decreases along \(\mathbf{E}\) and \(q > 0\), \(U\) decreases).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The electric potential energy of the positively charged particle decreases because the charge moves along the electric field.

ধাপ ১: মূল ধারণাগত নীতি
সুষম তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্র \(\mathbf{E}\)-তে স্থাপিত একটি ধনাত্মক আধান \(q > 0\) তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রের দিকেই \(\mathbf{F} = q\mathbf{E}\) স্থিরতড়িৎ বল অনুভব করে। এছাড়াও, তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রের অভিমুখে তড়িৎ বিভব \(V\) সর্বদা হ্রাস পায়।

ধাপ ২: মূল্যায়ন
যেহেতু কণাটিকে স্থির অবস্থা থেকে ছেড়ে দেওয়া হয়েছে, তাই এটি লব্ধি বলের দিকে অর্থাৎ তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্র \(\mathbf{E}\)-এর অভিমুখে ত্বরিত হয়ে গতিশীল হয়। কণাটি \(\mathbf{E}\)-এর দিকে অগ্রসর হওয়ার সাথে সাথে স্থিরতড়িৎ ক্ষেত্র আধানটির ওপর ধনাত্মক কার্য করে, ফলে এর গতিশক্তি বৃদ্ধি পায়।

ধাপ ৩: প্রয়োগ
স্থিরতড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রে যান্ত্রিক শক্তির সংরক্ষণ নীতি অনুযায়ী, গতিশক্তি বৃদ্ধির সমান পরিমাণে তড়িৎ স্থিতিশক্তি \(U = qV\) হ্রাস পায় (অনুরূপভাবে, \(\mathbf{E}\)-এর দিকে \(V\) হ্রাস পায় এবং \(q > 0\) হওয়ায় \(U\) হ্রাস পায়)।

ধাপ ৪: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
ধনাত্মক আধানটির তড়িৎ স্থিতিশক্তি হ্রাস পায় কারণ আধানটি তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রের অভিমুখে গতিশীল হয়।
